insight: Node.js 25.8 crypto API missing createCertificate and createSelfSignedSubject - use openssl CLI instead for certificate generation
@fastify/websocket doesn't export Socket type - use simple interface { remoteAddress?: string } for connection validation instead

The mid-panel widget system allows plugins to contribute UI elements to a horizontal bar in the TUI. Each widget needs an id, label, and getContent() function. Multiple widgets are rendered side-by-side with " │ " separators. The system is extensible - any plugin can offer a widget.

Phase 3.3 knowledge registry implementation went smoothly. The coordinator-beacon sync pattern (push/pull with upsert) is consistent with the existing persona/skill sync pattern, making integration straightforward.

The macros loader had no error handling around parseMacroFile() — any malformed .macro file would crash the entire agent during plugin initialization. The fix was to wrap the call in try-catch and log a warning, which is a pattern that should be applied more broadly across the plugin system.

The executeMacro function in the macros plugin had no error handling around substituteMacroArgs() — missing required args would throw and crash the agent mid-execution. The fix wraps each step in try-catch and logs a helpful message with usage info. This pattern of catching runtime errors in slash command handlers and showing usage hints is worth standardizing.

The macro plugin's executeMacro calls sendUserMessage without an onEvent callback, so all ConversationEvent emissions (reasoning, toolCall, toolResult, assistantMessage) are lost. The event type is defined in conversation-service.ts, not in drone-core, so plugins can't type-check it — they must use a runtime type guard. Consider exporting ConversationEvent from drone-core so plugins can handle events properly.

The TUI's runSlashCommand returns early when a slash command is handled by the engine, without ever calling setIsLlmActive(true). This means any slash command that triggers LLM work (like a macro with chatPrompt steps) won't show the working indicator. The fix is to wrap the dispatchSlashCommand call in setIsLlmActive(true/false).

The ConversationEvent type is defined in conversation-service.ts but not exported from drone-core. Plugins that need to handle events from sendUserMessage must use a runtime type guard (event as { kind?: string; ... }) instead of proper TypeScript types. Consider exporting ConversationEvent from drone-core for type-safe plugin event handling.

When planning distributed systems like the drone swarm, specifically addressing the ' la trace' (event-log) pattern vs. a simple 'state' pattern early on allows for much better support of later features like knowledge distillation and real-time monitoring.

Phase 3.2 shared session storage implementation: Added swarm_sessions and swarm_events tables with FTS5 to drone-coordinator, a file-based blob storage engine for large payloads (>10KB), REST API endpoints for session/event CRUD, beacon coordinator client methods for registerSwarmSession/pushEvents, and swarm plugin correlationId generation with push-through event buffering. The DroneLogger type lacks a debug() method, which required changing debug calls to info() in the swarm plugin.

The DroneLogger type in drone-core/src/session-types.ts only has info/warn/error methods but no debug method. This caused a type error when the swarm plugin tried to use logger.debug(). The fix was to use logger.info() instead. Consider adding debug() to DroneLogger for future use.

Phase 3.2 shared session storage demonstrated several reusable patterns: (1) Use FTS5 for full-text search in SQLite, (2) Content-addressable storage with SHA-256 hash references for large payloads (>10KB threshold), (3) Foreign key constraints to maintain SESSIONS→EVENTS relationship integrity, (4) CorrelationId (UUID v4) to link all events from a single user turn together.

Security architecture used Ed25519 keypairs for beacon identity, TLS for transport encryption, auto-approval for localhost beacons to simplify local development, and local-only WSS enforcement to restrict connections to localhost. Trust table model with approval tokens provides a simple but effective beacon authorization flow.

Macro UI feedback fix used event callback pattern to stream conversation events from sendUserMessage to the logger, with type guards to safely handle unknown event types. UI indicator activation (setIsLlmActive) should wrap any async dispatch that may trigger LLM calls for proper visual feedback.

Global memory/skills used confidence-based conflict resolution (keep highest confidence when same key from multiple sources), pull-based sync with optional push, and local caching for offline operation. Knowledge types (fact, preference, skill_pattern, principle) provide useful categorization for swarm-wide knowledge.

The persona-principles fragment exists in the code but was not rendering because: (1) it only reads from persona-specific principles files, ignoring project-level principles entirely, and (2) the rendering logic was scoped too narrowly. The combined fragment approach fixes this by scanning both project and persona principles directories.

The swarm learning feature (Phase 3.4) decomposes into four distinct parts: (1) swarm-wide insights/principles promotion via a storage broker pattern, (2) LLM Wiki-style knowledge base on beacon/coordinator servers, (3) beacon-only as an intentional scope boundary (not degradation), (4) migration tool for asset promotion/demotion. The clean separation between local scope (project/user, file-based) and swarm scope (beacon/coordinator, server-based) is the key architectural decision.

The self-improvement plugin refactoring to a broker pattern was more complex than expected because persona/skill definitions don't carry a `providerId` field. The routing approach had to be simplified to scope-based routing (check if target is beacon/coordinator-scoped, then look up the first registered engine) rather than provider-ID-based routing. This works but means only one swarm engine can be registered at a time. A future improvement could add a `providerId` field to persona/skill definitions for precise routing.

The coordinator-client.ts already had getBaseUrl() which was sufficient for the wiki proxy pattern in routes.ts. The wiki proxy uses a generic fetch-based approach via proxyWikiToCoordinator, so no additional client methods were needed.

The routes.ts files in beacon (1132 lines) and coordinator (808 lines) are overdue for splitting. Both follow the same pattern of domain-grouped route handlers. The beacon has additional complexity with shared state (coordinatorClient, proxy helpers) that needs to be extracted into a shared context module. The coordinator is simpler — no shared state, just direct db calls.

The beacon's routes were refactored from a single `routes.ts` into separate files in `routes/` directory. This is a good pattern but the `context.ts` module's `proxyToCoordinator` and `proxyWikiToCoordinator` functions are nearly identical — they could be consolidated into a single generic proxy function.

The plugin engine currently has no mechanism to add plugins after construction. The external plugin feature will need a new `addExternalPlugin()` method on the engine that adds a DronePlugin to the internal registry, registers it, and runs catch-up lifecycle hooks.

The external plugin loading feature required adding an `addExternalPlugin()` method to the engine because the existing `enablePlugin()` only works for plugins already in the registry. The new method adds the plugin to the registry map, registers it, and runs catch-up lifecycle hooks. This pattern could be useful for other dynamic plugin scenarios.

The migration service uses raw fetch() calls to the beacon HTTP API rather than going through the existing coordinator-client.ts. This is intentional for the standalone CLI tool (no engine needed), but means the migration service duplicates some HTTP logic. A future refactor could extract a shared HTTP client library.

Fastify 5.x type overloads are sensitive to the presence of the `https` property in the options object. Passing `https: undefined` still triggers the Http2SecureServer overload, causing type mismatches downstream. The fix is to use spread syntax (`...(cond ? { https: ... } : {})`) to conditionally include the property only when HTTPS is actually enabled.

The beacon-to-coordinator HTTPS connection fails because the coordinator uses a self-signed TLS cert and Node.js's built-in fetch() rejects it. The fix was to replace fetch() with a custom wrapper using http/https.request with rejectUnauthorized: false. A better long-term solution might be to have the beacon trust the coordinator's cert by fingerprint, or to use a shared CA.

When using Fastify with `https: { allowHTTP1: true }`, the server becomes an HTTP/2 secure server. For HTTP/2 secure servers, the TLS cert/key must be passed in the constructor's `https` property — NOT in `app.listen()`. Passing cert/key to `app.listen()` is silently ignored for HTTP/2 servers, causing the server to listen without a certificate and resulting in "SSL alert handshake failure" on the client side. The fix is to load the TLS identity before creating the Fastify instance and spread the cert/key into the `https` option in the constructor.

The @fastify/websocket WebSocket object (from the `ws` library) does not have a `remoteAddress` property — unlike raw Node.js sockets. The remote IP must be read from the Fastify `request` object (`request.ip` or `request.socket.remoteAddress`). The ws-server.ts was reading `socket.remoteAddress` which was always `undefined`, causing all WebSocket connections to be rejected as non-local.

The beacon and coordinator packages share significant code duplication (wiki-storage.ts, tls.ts, logger.ts are nearly identical). The test plan should test both copies independently, but a future refactoring opportunity exists to extract shared code into drone-core.

The coordinator's approveBeacon() function had a bug: after UPDATE set approval_token to NULL, the subsequent SELECT by approval_token would always fail. Fixed by querying beacon_id first, then looking up by beacon_id. This was caught by the new test suite.
The coordinator's FTS5 search query had a wrong column reference: `fts.id` should be `fts.rowid` for FTS5 virtual tables. This was a pre-existing bug in the source code that the new tests exposed.

The shadcn/ui "base-nova" style uses @base-ui/react instead of Radix, which means asChild prop is not supported on components like CollapsibleTrigger. Need to use plain elements instead of wrapping Button components.

The swarm plugin's event push-through mechanism was half-built: eventBuffer and flushEventBuffer exist, but nothing ever pushes events into the buffer. The onConversationEvent hook approach (new hook type in DronePluginHooks, dedicated engine method) is the cleanest way to wire it up — follows existing patterns like onSessionSafetyTrimWillRun.

The conversation event push-through was successfully wired up. The onConversationEvent hook pattern (new hook type in DronePluginHooks with a dedicated engine method) worked cleanly — the conversation service doesn't need to know about the swarm plugin, and the swarm plugin doesn't need access to the session manager. The fire-and-forget pattern with .catch() in the emit function prevents hook failures from blocking the conversation loop.

The beacon's sync.ts was missing proxy routes for /sync/events/push and /sync/sessions/register, causing 404 errors when the swarm plugin tried to push conversation events. The coordinator had the endpoints and the beacon's coordinator-client had the methods, but the beacon routes were never wired up. This is a pattern to watch for: when adding new swarm features, always check that the beacon proxy routes are created alongside the coordinator endpoints.

The coordinator's single-port architecture creates tension between API security (self-signed TLS) and browser usability (browsers reject self-signed certs). The dual-port approach (TLS for API, HTTP for UI) is a pragmatic solution, but the auth middleware only applies to /api/* and /ws — static files are always served without auth so the login page can load. This means the SPA JavaScript bundle is publicly accessible on the web port, which is fine since it contains no secrets.

The _runtime capability was gated behind the subagent plugin's offer() callback, but the subagent plugin never calls offer(). This is a fragile pattern — runtime options should be set unconditionally by the engine, not conditionally by a plugin that may or may not call offer().

Persona activation in onPluginsLoaded was too early for swarm-provided personas. The hook ordering guarantee (onPluginsLoaded fires in plugin registration order, onSessionStart fires after all onPluginsLoaded hooks) means cross-plugin coordination should use onSessionStart, not onPluginsLoaded.

When extracting shared code into a new workspace package, vitest's resolve aliases for sub-path imports (e.g., `drone-swarm-common/tls`) don't work reliably in tests that import from other packages. Tests in the consuming package had to use relative import paths instead. Consider adding `vite-tsconfig-paths` plugin or using a single root alias that re-exports everything.

The dot-separated tool name format (`plugin.tool`) causes degenerate behavior with Kimi K2 family models because their internal parser treats the dot as a structural separator in the `functions.{name}:{idx}` tool call ID format. This is a documented issue in the vLLM debugging blog and the Kimi K2 paper (Appendix B). The fix is to use a separator that only contains `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` characters, like `__`.

The broker+provider pattern with separate writer registration worked well for decoupling creation workflows from storage backends. The `exists` method on writers was a necessary addition to support the wizard's overwrite-check flow — it wasn't in the original plan but was required for correctness.

The `drone-migrate` bin stub was a dead import — it imported the module but never called any function. The `migrate.ts` module is designed as a library (exports only, no side effects), so the bin stub needs to explicitly wire args to `runMigrate()`. The `parseCliArgs` function requires a `'migrate'` prefix in argv to route to the migrate subcommand parser, which the standalone bin doesn't have naturally — it must prepend it.

The coordinator's FTS5 virtual table on swarm_events has a bug: it uses content_rowid='id' but id is a TEXT PRIMARY KEY, not an integer rowid. FTS5 requires an integer rowid for content tables. This should be fixed as part of the session pipeline work since we'll be querying events more heavily.

The coordinator's WebSocket auth check in index.ts doesn't mirror the onRequest hook's local-IP bypass logic in web-auth.ts. The onRequest hook trusts Tailscale IPs (100.64.0.0/10) as local, but the WebSocket handler's token check doesn't skip for those IPs. This causes immediate disconnect for Tailscale-connected clients. The fix is to reuse isLocalRequest in the WebSocket handler.

The swarm persona system has a fundamental type mismatch between persistence (Persona.systemPrompt) and runtime (DronePersonaDefinition.systemPromptOverride). The raw type cast in swarm/index.ts silently drops all rich frontmatter fields. This pattern (raw type cast between different types with overlapping but differently-named fields) is fragile and should be avoided — always map explicitly between persistence and runtime types.

The fix for swarm persona contents used parsePersonaMd() from the persona loader plugin, which is a cross-plugin import (swarm importing from persona). This works because both are built-in plugins in the same package, but it creates a coupling between plugins. A cleaner long-term solution would be to expose a parsePersonaMd capability through the persona broker's capability interface, so any plugin can parse persona .md content without a direct import.

The `tryMatchContext` function needed to try two edit positions (at the anchor and after it) to handle both cases where the anchor IS the line being replaced and where the anchor is context above the edit. This was a subtle design issue that only showed up in edge case tests (single-line file).

The file__apply_diff V2 tool has a critical bug in narrowByAnchors cascade: after exact-match narrowing (level 0) fails, the empty candidates array is passed to fuzzy fallback calls (level 1 and 100), making them no-ops. The first-anchor search correctly searches from scratch for each level, but the anchor chain narrowing does not preserve the initial candidates.

file__apply_diff v2 had a subtle cascade bug in narrowByAnchors: the candidates array was destructively reassigned on each fuzz level attempt. Fix was to snapshot firstAnchorCandidates before narrowing, so fuzzy fallbacks retry from the original state. This pattern (save state before cascade) should be used whenever implementing progressive-matching fallbacks.

React 19 types removed the global `JSX` namespace. All `JSX.Element` return type annotations must be changed to `React.JSX.Element` (with a `import type React from 'react'` if React isn't already imported as a value). This affects ~14 files in the TUI layer and any .tsx test files.

The file__apply_diff tool's nested JSON hunk format (array of objects with arrays of strings) is confusing the LLM. Switching to a flat unified diff string format should improve LLM reliability, but revisits ADR #033's decision about JSON schema vs freeform text — the pragmatic observation is that LLMs produce valid unified diff strings more reliably than valid nested JSON structures.

The unified diff format for file__apply_diff turned out well. Key lesson: ADR #033's argument that "JSON schema is better because we can constrain the output format" was technically correct but pragmatically wrong — LLMs produce valid unified diff strings far more reliably than valid nested JSON arrays-of-objects. The learning is: prefer flat, well-known text formats (like git diff) over custom nested JSON schemas for LLM tool inputs, even when parsing is slightly harder on the backend.

The conversation loop's concurrency gap (fire-and-forget TUI onSubmit vs sequential readline mode) has been documented and a plan for a queue+boundary-drain pattern is in place. The soft-cancel design via /cancel and ESC provides a clean exit without needing AbortController plumbing through LLM providers.

Cancel tests needed synchronous flag-setting inside tool execution, not setTimeout(fn, 0), because the cancel check in the while(true) loop fires before the event loop unwinds. Async scheduling doesn't work for cancel tests — the flag must be set synchronously within the tool execution callback.

The coordinator's messages.ts relay/broadcast routes use raw global fetch() to reach beacons. The user indicated fetch won't remain there much longer. Route tests should assert on observable behavior (status codes, delivered counts) rather than fetch call internals, to survive the eventual refactor.

Neither drone-coordinator nor drone-beacon calls setKnowledgeBaseDir(), so both default to wiki-storage's hardcoded './knowledge-base' relative to cwd. Since a coordinator host must co-locate a beacon, running both from one directory makes them overwrite each other's wiki. Plans A/B anchor the wiki under each service's config dir and change default config dirs to ~/.drone-coordinator and ~/.drone-beacon.

drone-coordinator/src/index.ts runs main() at import time and keeps setupServer private, blocking any fastify.inject() route testing. bin/drone-coordinator imports dist/index.js (not run-as-argv[1]), so a naive import.meta/argv entry guard would silently prevent the server from starting — the bin wrapper must call an exported main() explicitly. This entry/harness pattern likely applies to drone-beacon too (also has no route tests).

The coordinator's spawn route follows the exact same pattern as the message relay route (messages.ts) — two-step lookup (beaconId → host:port), plain fetch() forwarding, and the same error code conventions (BEACON_NOT_FOUND, BEACON_UNAVAILABLE). This consistency makes the codebase easy to extend.

Created drone-gateway package scaffold with CONTEXT.md, following the same patterns as drone-coordinator and drone-beacon (ESM, pino logger, tsconfig.base.json, bin/ entry point). The engine.ts has placeholder createAdapter/createControlSurface methods that throw — these will be replaced by actual implementations in follow-up phases (4.2-4.7). The coordinator-client.ts mirrors the spawn/beacon/agent endpoints from the coordinator's web port.

Expanded the gateway-core-plan to include standalone mode (no beacon/coordinator), persistent agent sessions via --output-json without --once, a turnComplete NDJSON event, a shared spawner in drone-swarm-common, and a pluggable SpawnBackend interface. The plan now covers both standalone and swarm modes for the gateway.

The vitest alias resolution doesn't handle subpath exports (e.g., `drone-swarm-common/spawner`) the same way as the main entry. The beacon's spawner wrapper had to import from `drone-swarm-common` (main entry) instead of `drone-swarm-common/spawner` (subpath export) for tests to work, even though the subpath export is defined in package.json for production builds. The vitest config alias was also needed.

When adding event streaming for conversation events, always route through the engine's conversation event hooks rather than through the DroneLogger interface. The logger only has info/warn/error levels, which loses color differentiation in the TUI. The engine hooks preserve event kind information and work for all sources (regular messages, macro chatPrompt steps, etc.) through a single listener.

The TUI tail region refactor plan identifies a subtle closure issue: the conversation event listener in app.tsx captures `scheme` from the render cycle, but scheme changes when color overrides cycle. The tail components need to read the current scheme from a ref or context, not from the closure, to avoid stale color references in live-updating components.

The tail region refactor revealed a subtle closure issue with `scheme` (color scheme) in the conversation event listener. Since `scheme` changes when color overrides cycle on a timer, capturing it in the useEffect closure would cause stale color references. Fixed by using a `useRef` for the scheme that gets updated on every render (`schemeRef.current = scheme`), and having the listener read from the ref.

The `toEntry()` function on TailItem was initially typed to return `ChatEntry` (with `id`), but this conflicted with `useChatLog`'s `log()` and `appendEntry()` which expect `Omit<ChatEntry, 'id'>` and generate the id internally. Changed `toEntry()` to return `Omit<ChatEntry, 'id'>` to match the existing pattern and avoid duplicate id generation.

When a class is imported via dynamic `await import(...)`, the destructured binding is a value, not a type. You can't use it directly as a type annotation (`let x: ClassName` errors). The clean fix is `InstanceType<typeof ClassName>` — it reads the instance type from the value without needing a separate `import type` that would conflict with the local binding.

The TUI app.tsx event listener hardcodes special-case formatting for specific tools (exec__run, file__apply_diff, git__diff) via formatExecResult/formatDiffResult/formatToolResult. This is brittle — every new tool with custom display needs a new special case. The planned renderComponent pattern on DroneToolDefinition eliminates this by letting plugins own their rendering.

The renderComponent pattern requires engine.getTool() to be available in the TUI's event listener. This was already implemented in the engine for other purposes but wasn't exposed through DroneTuiOptions. Needed to add it to the Pick<> type. Always check if a dependency already exists at a lower layer before creating a new path.

db-helpers.ts in drone-swarm-common used `any` for the better-sqlite3 Database type to avoid adding it as a dependency. Replaced with minimal local structural interfaces (Database, Statement) that match only the subset of the API we use — clean pattern for shared packages that wrap a dependency of their consumers.

The MCP streamable-HTTP client's `disconnect` is typed `() => void` (sync) while `DELETE` session termination is inherently async. The point-8 plan works around this by firing the `DELETE` best-effort (fire-and-forget, `.catch`-logged) to respect the sync signature. A future refactor could make `JsonRpcClient.disconnect` return `Promise<void>` for both stdio and HTTP transports so graceful termination can be awaited by `onShutdown`.

In the MCP streamable-HTTP client, the fire-and-forget GET SSE reader (void openGetStream()) can report a stream error before the caller has assigned its connection handle. The index.ts wiring uses a `let connection` declared before the loop with an `if (connection)` guard, and unit tests must mirror this with a holder. Any future code that reacts to onStreamError during connect must account for the connection handle possibly not existing yet.

When validating a plan's "pnpm build green" gate, check the GLOBAL build baseline, not just your own diff. On 2026-07-08 the repo's `pnpm build` was already RED at session start (pre-existing, untouched files: drone-core/src/index.ts omitted the `DroneElicitation` re-export, causing TS2305/TS7006 in elicitation.ts, external-loader.ts, persona/wizard.ts, skills/wizard.ts, runtime/plugin-engine.ts, tui/elicitation.ts). These matched the session's initial LSP diagnostics exactly. Fixing the one-line re-export was necessary and safe; it also resolves the downstream `implicitly any` errors. Confirm pre-existing breakage by stashing only your own changed files and rebuilding.

The dependabot PR bundled two unrelated dependency bumps (vitest 2→3 and matrix-js-sdk 34→38) in a single commit, making it harder to isolate and fix the resulting test failures. Dependabot groups should be reviewed more carefully, or the npm_and_yarn group should be split to avoid bundling unrelated major version bumps.

unregisterPluginToolsImpl in plugin-engine.ts had a subtle bug: it only iterated over the plugin's static tool list (registered during register()), but the MCP plugin registers tools dynamically via registerTool() at runtime. Those dynamic tools were never cleaned up, causing "Tool already registered" errors on re-mount. Fixed by iterating the tools map by prefix instead.

The plugin engine lacks a single-tool unregister method — it only has `unregisterPluginTools(pluginId)` which bulk-removes all tools for a plugin. The MCP list/mount pattern requires `unregisterTool(canonicalName)` for unmounting individual dynamically-mounted tools. This is a gap in the engine API that should be addressed as part of the list/mount plan.
